items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: That of course is Johnny Wiggs and his New Orleans Kings. The vocal was done by Dr. Edmund Sushon.

ctx.x: In a house, in a square, in a quadrant, in a street, in a lane, in a road. Turn to the left on the right hand, you'll see there my true love's a bone. I go there according and going to my love like a turtle dove. And it's wearing on my bending knee, if ever I cease to love. May the sheep's head grow on apple trees, if ever I cease to love. If ever I cease to love, yes, if ever I cease to love. May the moon be turned to green, green cheese, if ever I cease to love. 된된 된 ! The End
The End That of course is Johnny Wiggs and his New Orleans Kings. The vocal was done by Dr. Edmund Sushon. Mr. Wiggs, how long ago was that recorded, sir?
I guess about 12 years or 15 years, wasn't it, Dick? Seems to me it was about 15 years ago. You were at that session, weren't you?

items.title: Edmond "Doc" Souchon Interview, 1962-02-17
items.q: You can hear that on those records that Johnny had him to record.

ctx.x: And it just messed me up. I couldn't get that stroke. Now, Thompson McKay, there were two brothers, Percy and Thompson. Percy is one of the vice presidents of the Whitney Bank. Thompson's a consulting engineer in Dallas for one of the very big engineering firms. He was better than Percy and he had that Negro style down pat. He played just exactly like they did in the cornfield plantation stuff. Now, the best guitarist that I ever heard any place, and I don't think there'll ever be one before or after, no matter…
You can hear that on those records that Johnny had him to record. Yes, indeed. Did he do much better than that? Those are plenty good.
Well, yes, he did much better than that.
